_comment: Phase 5 versioned evaluation dataset. Extends v1 (same 3 clips, GT-001..GT-003, Q1..Q4 preserved verbatim where possible) with per-example recording linkage, video-relative boundaries, absolute timestamps, evidence references, negative/ambiguous/temporal queries, and labeled cross-camera associations. ALL footage is synthetic FFmpeg color blocks — see limitations.

footage_provenance.generator: FFmpeg color-block synthetic videos (see v1 methodology)
footage_provenance.real_footage_note: No real labeled CCTV footage was available for Phase 5. All metrics below measure performance on synthetic color-block clips only and MUST NOT be presented as real-world CCTV performance.

events.description: Red rectangular figure (synthetic person proxy) visible near the entrance.
events.absolute_time_note: Reliable only because the clip is synthetic with a declared recording start; not representative of real CCTV clock accuracy.
events.limitation_notes: Color block is a proxy, not a person. No occlusion, low-light, or timestamp-uncertainty coverage.

events.description: Blue rectangular object (synthetic bag/package proxy) visible in the hallway.
events.absolute_time_note: Reliable only because the clip is synthetic with a declared recording start; not representative of real CCTV clock accuracy.
events.limitation_notes: Whether this is the 'same entity' as GT-001 cannot be determined from color blocks; any identity link is speculative.

events.description: Green rectangular shape (synthetic vehicle proxy) visible in the parking lot.
events.absolute_time_note: Reliable only because the clip is synthetic with a declared recording start; not representative of real CCTV clock accuracy.
events.limitation_notes: No cross-camera match expected: disjoint appearance, disjoint event type, large temporal gaps.

queries.notes: Time filter uses video-relative seconds (00:00-00:15 -> 0-15s). V1 expectation preserved: only GT-001. KNOWN BEHAVIOR GAP (kept as temporal regression case): investigate() scores temporal queries by leftover keyword terms ('all','00','15') instead of treating them as pure time filters, so on the deterministic fixture Q4 returns [GT-002] via the substring 'all' in 'hallway' (precision 0, recall 0). The v1 live run returned all three events (precision 1/3) because real-model text matched more terms. Expectation encodes intent (pure time filter), not current implementation.
Negative case: nothing in the dataset matches. Any returned event is a false positive. Tests empty-prediction handling.

Ambiguous case: vague description ('dark', 'figure', 'carrying') fits no GT event exactly but is plausibly near GT-001/GT-002. Predictions matching ambiguous events are reported separately and excluded from precision/recall.

Temporal filter regression: GT midpoints 5.5 (in), 8.5 (out), 4.0 (in). Uses video-relative seconds. Expectation encodes intent (pure time filter). KNOWN GAP: leftover keyword terms ('all','00','06') dominate scoring, so the deterministic fixture returns [] (recall 0) — same root cause as Q4.
Temporal negative: all GT midpoints (5.5, 8.5, 4.0) fall outside 12-15s. Any returned event is a false positive.

cross_camera_associations._comment: Unordered GT-id pairs. Identity can never be confirmed from synthetic color blocks, so no pair is labeled valid.
cross_camera_associations.valid_note: Empty by design: no same-entity evidence exists for synthetic color blocks. Cross-camera recall is therefore undefined (null) on this dataset; only false-association behavior is measurable.

invalid.reason: Disjoint appearance (red figure vs green vehicle), disjoint event types, ~60s temporal gap. Must NOT link.
Disjoint appearance (blue object vs green vehicle), disjoint event types, ~65s temporal gap. Must NOT link. Regression case for the 4 false associations in eval_results.json (2026-10-28).

ambiguous.reason: Temporal proximity (117s gap, within the 300s correlator window) but disjoint appearance descriptions and disjoint event types. V1 listed these as cross_camera_candidate; v2 downgrades to AMBIGUOUS because visually similar/dissimilar color blocks can neither confirm nor refute identity. Links here are reported separately, never scored as correct.

expected_gaps: The parking camera event should NOT produce a cross-camera link to the entrance or hallway cameras (different event type, large temporal gap, no shared appearance tokens).

match_rules.window_rule: A prediction matches a GT event when |pred_ts - gt_midpoint| <= (gt_half_window + time_tolerance_seconds).
match_rules.keyword_rule: Prediction text (action_description + observed_facts + object_descriptions + scene_description, lowercased) must contain at least keyword_overlap_min of the GT expected_keywords.
match_rules.assignment: Greedy 1:1 assignment: GT events in id order take the lowest-timestamp-error unmatched prediction satisfying all rules.

known_limitations: ALL footage is synthetic FFmpeg color blocks; results do NOT represent real-world CCTV performance.
No real labeled footage was available; no real annotations were created or invented.
Tiny sample: 3 GT events, 8 queries. Per-event-type statistics are reported with sample counts and flagged low-sample (n<5).
No coverage for occlusion, low light, incomplete footage, unsynchronized camera clocks, or timestamp uncertainty (synthetic timestamps are exact).
No confirmed-valid cross-camera pair exists, so cross-camera recall is undefined; only false-association rate is measurable.
Q4/Q7/Q8 encode pure-time-filter intent, but investigate() scores leftover keyword terms; see per-query notes for the observed behavior gap.

methodology.clip_generation: FFmpeg color-block synthetic videos. No real individuals, no real locations.
methodology.model_dependency: Results depend on vision model output. With MockMetaClient, all frames return empty objects[] — most events will not be detected. Real model required for meaningful precision/recall.
known_limitations: Color blocks are not realistic CCTV footage — real models may describe them differently or not at all.
Event grouping depends on model returning objects in the same frames as the colored blocks appear.
Cross-camera correlation depends on shared appearance tokens (e.g. 'red', 'blue') — if model uses different words, links will not form.
